name: bold typographic poster
brief: Type is the hero: an oversized headline fills most of the frame on a solid brand colour field, with at most a small, cropped photographic or graphic accent. Strong contrast, tight leading, the key points as a clean stack beneath.

name: editorial photo with colour panel
brief: A candid documentary photograph on one part of the frame and a solid colour panel on the rest carrying the headline and points, separated by a thin rule. Restrained, magazine-like, generous margins.

name: split screen
brief: The frame split into two halves or thirds: one a real photograph, the other a flat colour block with huge numerals or a single large statement. A deliberate asymmetric split, not a centred layout.

name: flat vector illustration
brief: A clean, modern flat vector illustration in a limited palette built from the brand colours: simple geometric people, devices and shapes telling the idea, with the text set in a bold sans on calm areas. No photographs.

name: isometric scene
brief: A tidy isometric illustration with soft shadows: stacked blocks, screens, flows and small figures that visualise the idea, with the headline set large above and the points on clean labels. Light background, brand-coloured objects.

name: interface collage
brief: Cropped, slightly tilted plain software interface panels (cards, charts, lists with abstract content, no readable text on them) layered with soft shadows over a brand colour background, with the headline and points as large type beside or over them.

name: duotone photo with oversized type
brief: One striking photograph treated in a two-colour brand duotone, filling the frame, with an oversized headline overlaid in white or the lightest tone and the points in a tidy column. Cinematic, high contrast.

name: cutout collage
brief: A person or object cut out from a photograph and placed over bold flat geometric shapes in brand colours, with a slightly paper-cut feel. The headline in heavy type that interacts with the shapes; points on small clean tags.

name: blueprint line drawing
brief: A refined technical line drawing on a deep blue or off-white grid: diagrams, nodes and flows drawn in thin lines with a single accent colour, headline in a confident sans, points as annotated callouts. Precise and calm, never childish.

name: swiss grid minimal
brief: A strict grid with a lot of white space: one huge numeral or word, a small photograph or shape, perfectly aligned text blocks, a single accent colour. Quiet, premium, very legible.

name: magazine cover
brief: A business magazine cover feel: a large masthead-like headline over a full-bleed photograph, with the key points as short cover lines at the sides. Use only the given words: no masthead name, tag line, issue number or label of your own. Confident and editorial.

name: soft gradient cards
brief: A smooth modern gradient background in brand colours with frosted-glass style cards holding the headline and each point, subtle depth, rounded corners. Contemporary software-brand look, calm and clean.
